findings.summary: The P3/P4 lead-pipeline seeds (pnpm seed:lead-pipeline, pnpm seed:icp-acqu) are documented nowhere — the launch doc's seed sequence omits them, so an operator following the doc launches with no discovery/enrichment agents and no active ICP.
findings.detail: Step 2.6's seed list (connect-and-launch.md:89-98) covers seed:acqu-vitals, phase-1..4, phase-9, tool-browser but not the lead-pipeline seeds that root package.json exposes (package.json:31-32 — seed:lead-pipeline, seed:icp-acqu → scripts/seed/seed-lead-pipeline.ts and icp-acqu-starter.ts). grep across docs/, README.md, and LAUNCH.md finds zero mentions of either command. The launch-readiness operator-gated printout (scripts/launch-readiness/launch-readiness.ts:215-220) also never mentions them. Consequence: the Phase-69 CR-01 fix makes discovery dispatch load the tenant's active ICP server-side — with icp-acqu never seeded there is no active ICP, so the pipeline the last two phases hardened is unreachable for anyone following the documented launch path. core/lead-pipeline (pure helpers) is the only P3/P4 gate in launch:check; nothing gates or documents the seeds.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `pnpm seed:lead-pipeline` and `pnpm seed:icp-acqu` to the Step 2.6 seed block (with one line each: what they seed and that icp-acqu creates the active ICP the discovery agent's dispatch gate requires). Mirror them in docs/internal-launch-runbook.md and in launch-readiness.ts's operator-gated printout.

findings.summary: OFFLINE_TESTS omits verified-offline safety suites — runner test:cantfail (runtime cantfail.model_violation assertion), runner test:execute-flow, runner test (custom-tools incl. the Phase-69 update_lead guards), core test:immutability, core test:security — so a regression in any of them still reports READY.
findings.detail: The header (L3-20) claims the script 'asserts every offline launch invariant', but the 24-entry battery includes only 1 of the runner's 12 suites (test:lease-integration) and 22 of ~40 core suites. Spot-checked headers confirm the omitted ones are offline: apps/runner/src/cantfail.test.ts ('No live model, no live DB' — the SessionStart T-critical Opus assertion), apps/runner/src/execute-flow.test.ts (dryRun, covers cantfail/CRA/budget/autonomy ratchet), apps/runner/src/custom-tools.test.ts ('No live model, no live network' — contains the Phase-69 CR-02 tool.lead.update_lead whitelist/tenant/shape guard tests at L165-207), packages/core/src/architect/hydrate.immutability.test.ts (pins CANT_FAIL_KEYS membership + hydrate refusal), packages/core/src/security/findings.test.ts + anomaly.test.ts ('no live DB'). Also offline and absent: core test:mirror, test:waved, test:parity, test:intelligence, test:intelligent-pick, test:model-feedback, test:cost-forecast, test:task-profile-inference, test:tenant-cap, test:model-suggestion, test:scorecard, test:controller, test:job, test:hydrate-restart. The launch gate's own section 5 regex-counts CANT_FAIL_KEYS but does not run the suite that asserts the runner enforces it at dispatch.
findings.fix_sketch: Append the offline runner suites to OFFLINE_TESTS ({ label: 'runner/cantfail', filter: '@agent-os/runner', script: 'test:cantfail' }, execute-flow, predispatch, custom-tools via script 'test', budget, cap-breach-flow, delegate, run-state, sub-agent, system-prompt, artifact-emit) and the omitted offline core suites (test:security, test:immutability, router/eval suites). Alternatively generate the list from each package.json's test:* scripts with an explicit DB-required exclusion set, so the gate can't drift from reality again.

findings.summary: Template ships a non-empty DATABASE_URL default pointing at database `postgres`, while docker-compose provisions `agentos` — migrations land in the wrong DB, and the non-empty default makes setup.ts treat the DB as configured even when the operator explicitly skipped it.
findings.detail: Two failure modes from one default. (a) Wrong DB name: docker-compose.yml:34 creates POSTGRES_DB=agentos and every doc (docker-compose.yml:12-16, docs/connect-and-launch.md:60) says to use .../agentos — but the template default is postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres. The `postgres` maintenance DB always exists in the container, so `pnpm db:migrate` with the template default silently succeeds against the wrong database; the operator then connects to /agentos per the docs and finds zero tables (isolation suite and seeds fail confusingly). (b) setup wizard contradiction: scripts/setup/setup.ts:249 does `if (env.get("DATABASE_URL"))` and reportCheck (setup.ts:161,168) does `.length > 0` — both always truthy because buildEnvFromTemplate keeps the non-empty template default when the operator answers No to Supabase. So the wizard prints '→ Skipped. UI runs on demo data until DATABASE_URL is set' (L235) immediately followed by 'pnpm db:migrate # push 32 migrations to Supabase' + seed + verify:isolation-live (L255-257), and `pnpm setup:check` shows '✓ DATABASE_URL' on a fresh skip.
findings.fix_sketch: Ship DATABASE_URL= (empty) in .env.example and move the localhost example into the comment as `# e.g. postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/agentos (matches docker-compose)`. If a non-empty default must stay, use the /agentos db name and teach setup.ts to treat the known template default as 'not configured' (compare against the template value before printing live-DB next steps / ✓).

findings.summary: Step 6 Path B claims 'the platform's connection interface will detect Nango env vars and route connector OAuth through it instead of the vault' — no code reads NANGO_SECRET_KEY / NANGO_PUBLIC_KEY / NANGO_HOST anywhere; the only Nango reference is a stub comment.
findings.detail: grep across apps/, packages/, scripts/ for NANGO_* finds zero reads; the sole 'nango' hit is a doc-comment in packages/core/src/security/refreshers/stubs.ts:3. Yet .env.example:91-96 offers the three vars and connect-and-launch.md:215-226 walks the operator through minting Nango keys and states present-tense detection behavior. An operator preparing external-tenant posture sets the keys, sees no error, and believes connector OAuth is routed through Nango while every credential still flows through the vault — a silent security-posture misunderstanding in the launch doc. CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 frames Nango as the *client-launch* posture, so the doc is describing planned work as shipped.
findings.fix_sketch: Until the detection lands, mark both surfaces honestly: in connect-and-launch.md change to 'PLANNED — not yet implemented; the connection interface currently always uses the vault', and add the same note above the NANGO_ block in .env.example (or drop the block until the integration exists). When implemented, wire the env detection where connections are created (apps/api /api/connections/:mcpId/credential path).

findings.summary: Smoke has no unauthenticated GET /health probe and covers 8 of ~20 admin GET endpoints despite claiming to confirm 'the shape of every load-bearing admin endpoint' — when the service is down or the admin key is wrong, all 8 checks fail identically with no liveness/auth separation.
findings.detail: apps/api/src/index.ts:110 exposes GET /health with no auth — the natural first probe — but CHECKS starts straight at authenticated admin endpoints, so a dead service, a wrong AOS_BASE_URL, and a revoked AOS_ADMIN_KEY all produce the same 8-failure wall. Uncovered admin GET surfaces that the header comment implies are in scope: /api/admin/scorecards (:560), /api/admin/scorecards/latest (:652), /api/admin/models/proposals (:1083), /api/admin/architect/blueprints (:1138), /api/admin/artifacts/recent (:1022), /api/admin/runs/:runId/artifacts (:952), /api/connections (:1692). No endpoint exists for the lead pipeline, so no smoke gap there — but the doc-comment overclaims relative to the 8 checks.
findings.fix_sketch: Prepend two probes: (1) unauthenticated GET /health expecting 200 — abort the run with a clear 'service unreachable' message if it fails; (2) an auth canary (any admin GET) that distinguishes 401/403 ('bad AOS_ADMIN_KEY') from shape failures. Then add the missing admin GETs to CHECKS, or soften the header comment to name the exact 8 endpoints covered.

findings.summary: Phase-69-deferred INFO-02: require("@agent-os/db") inside ESM lazy DB getter, plus a second getDb singleton duplicating custom-tools.ts
findings.detail: createDbLazy (lines 764-770) calls require() in an ESM module (root package.json has "type":"module"); it only works under tsx's CJS shim and breaks under strict ESM. The justifying comment ("kept lazy so the module doesn't require DATABASE_URL at import time") is moot: line 19 already imports { schema, type Db } from "@agent-os/db" at module top, and importing the createDb function reads no env — only calling it does. Separately, custom-tools.ts:72-79 already has a proper getDb() (top-level createDb import at custom-tools.ts:44, lazy connection on first call), so the runner process now holds TWO independent lazy DB singletons/postgres pools (custom-tools cachedDb + lead-pipeline _db). Note: lead-pipeline-tools.ts imports only a type from custom-tools.js (line 34, erased at compile), while custom-tools.ts value-imports LEAD_PIPELINE_TOOLS (line 209) — importing getDb as a value from custom-tools would create a runtime import cycle, so consolidation should go through a new shared module.
findings.fix_sketch: Minimal: add createDb to the existing line-19 import from "@agent-os/db", delete createDbLazy and the require() (lines 764-770), keep the getDb() lazy singleton. Better: extract apps/runner/src/db.ts exporting one lazy getDb() (top-level createDb import, cached connection, error message "DATABASE_URL required for runner tool dispatch"), and have both custom-tools.ts:72-79 and lead-pipeline-tools.ts:756-770 use it — one pool, no cycle, no require().

findings.summary: tool.vault-rotate accepts an agent-supplied mcpId with no tenant-ownership check — cross-tenant OAuth credential rotation is possible
findings.detail: The handler at apps/runner/src/custom-tools.ts:183-192 passes `input.mcpId` straight to rotateCredential() without validating that the MCP belongs to ctx.tenantId (which IS available — the dispatcher sets it from bundle.agent.tenantId at line 477). rotateCredential (packages/core/src/security/vault-rotate.ts:44-48) selects oauth_credentials by `eq(oauthCredentials.mcpId, mcpId)` alone — no tenant predicate — then decrypts the stored tokens with the shared AOS_VAULT_KEY and calls the provider refresher. A prompt-injected or off-prompt agent that emits another tenant's mcpId (UUIDs leak via relay events, findings payloads, artifacts) rotates THAT tenant's credential: the provider refresh invalidates the old refresh-token chain, and the rotated token is written back under cred.tenantId — a cross-tenant write to vault secrets. The only mitigation is the tool-level requiresApproval=true, but the operator approving sees an opaque UUID and cannot tell it is cross-tenant. This violates CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #2 (tenant isolation 'including the runner's view'). Every lead-pipeline handler in the same dispatch table was hardened to derive tenant from ctx for exactly this reason; these Phase 9 handlers predate that pattern. No test covers a cross-tenant mcpId refusal (custom-tools.test.ts only tests update_lead tenant guards; vault-rotate.test.ts is a mock-db unit test).
findings.fix_sketch: In the tool.vault-rotate handler: require ctx.tenantId, then before calling rotateCredential, load the mcp scoped to tenant — `db.select({id: schema.mcps.id}).from(schema.mcps).where(and(eq(schema.mcps.id, mcpId), eq(schema.mcps.tenantId, ctx.tenantId))).limit(1)` — and return a refusal envelope if absent. Belt-and-braces: add a `tenantId` parameter to rotateCredential and add `eq(oauthCredentials.tenantId, tenantId)` to its where clause, so the core function fails closed even for future callers.

findings.summary: tool.access-audit and tool.access-log-analyzer take tenantId from agent-supplied input, not ctx — agent-triggerable cross-tenant reads
findings.detail: At apps/runner/src/custom-tools.ts:193-202 both handlers do `const { tenantId } = input as { tenantId: string }` and pass the agent-supplied value to findOrphanedGrants / detectUsageSpikes, which faithfully scope their SQL to that tenant_id (packages/core/src/security/access-audit.ts:34, anomaly.ts:38,45). ctx.tenantId (from bundle.agent.tenantId, set at custom-tools.ts:477) is ignored. Any agent bound to these tools — and provisionClientTenant clones the template workforce, so client tenants can inherit them — can pass another tenant's UUID and receive that tenant's data back into its own run context: credential ids, mcp ids/names, agent keys and lifecycle states (access-audit), and per-tool usage patterns (log-analyzer). tool.access-audit is seeded with requiresApproval=false (scripts/seed/acqu-access-auditor.ts:42), so there is no human gate. This is a direct break of the stated invariant 'a cross-tenant read must return zero rows — including the runner's view' (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #2 / hard gate #2). The existing tests (access-audit.test.ts, anomaly.test.ts) only assert rendered-SQL shape, not the tenantId provenance, so no gate covers this.
findings.fix_sketch: Derive tenant from ctx and refuse mismatches: `if (!ctx.tenantId) return envelope-error; const tenantId = ctx.tenantId;` and drop tenantId from the accepted input entirely (or, if operators need explicit input for cron parity, require `input.tenantId === ctx.tenantId` and refuse otherwise). Mirror the guard shape used by the lead-pipeline handlers ('requires tenant context'). Add a custom-tools.test.ts case asserting a foreign tenantId in input is refused.

findings.summary: apify_run_actor's CR-01 matrix gate fails OPEN for actor ids not in DISCOVERY_ACTORS — arbitrary unregistered Apify actors can still be dispatched
findings.detail: The Phase 69 CR-01 fix (lines 93-113) loads the active ICP and refuses mismatched target_types, but only inside `if (matrixActor) { ... }`. When the agent passes an actor_id that matches neither `key` nor `externalId` of any DISCOVERY_ACTORS entry, matrixActor is undefined: the gate is skipped entirely, `externalId = actor_id` (line 121) forwards the raw string to Apify, and the cap falls back to 100 items (line 117). So the doctrine rule the gate implements ('never run an actor whose targets[] excludes the ICP's targetType' — lead-pipeline.ts:63-65; an unregistered actor lists NO targets) is bypassable by any off-matrix actor id, and the discovery prompt's promise that 'the tool will reject mismatched runs' is again false for exactly the inputs most likely to be hallucinated or injected. Operator pays for arbitrary actor runs on APIFY_TOKEN and lead provenance records unregistered source_actor keys.
findings.fix_sketch: Fail closed: after the find(), `if (!matrixActor) return envErr(`actor ${actor_id} not in DISCOVERY_ACTORS — only registered actors are dispatchable`);` then run the ICP target_type check unconditionally. If ad-hoc actors are a deliberate escape hatch, gate them behind an explicit operator flag (e.g. AOS_ALLOW_UNREGISTERED_APIFY_ACTORS=1) rather than default-open.

findings.summary: update_lead does not enforce the hard-disqualifier doctrine server-side: an agent can write qualified=true with dnc_flag=true or email_status='invalid'; enum fields are also unvalidated
findings.detail: The doctrine (lead-pipeline.ts:13 'DNC or invalid email always disqualifies, regardless of score') is implemented in applyQualificationRules, but that pure function is never invoked server-side — grep shows it is only exported and unit-tested. updateLead accepts agent-supplied `qualified` (line 501) and derives status='qualified' from it (lines 508-510) without cross-checking dnc_flag/email_status in the same patch or on the existing row (the ownership select at 481-485 only reads id+status). A single off-prompt tool call `{lead_id, icp_score: 90, qualified: true, dnc_flag: true}` produces a status='qualified', dnc_flag=true lead — the exact suppression-violating row outreach must never pick up, and a compliance exposure once outreach lands. Secondarily, email_status/phone_type/dnc_flag pass through with zero shape validation (lines 502-504): a non-enum string hits the DB CHECK constraint (migration 0032:75-78) and throws a raw exception out of the handler instead of the clean `{ok:false}` envelope every other invalid input gets.
findings.fix_sketch: Extend the ownership select to also read dnc_flag + email_status; merge with the incoming patch; then run applyQualificationRules (or minimally: `if (effectiveDnc || effectiveEmailStatus === 'invalid') { patch.qualified = false; patch.status = 'disqualified'; }`) before building setValues. Validate email_status against the EmailStatus union, phone_type against PhoneType, and `typeof raw.dnc_flag === 'boolean'` in the fail-fast block (lines 462-476) so garbage returns envErr instead of a DB CHECK exception.

findings.summary: V2 sink writes update approvals/objectives/leases by bare id with no tenant predicate — the uniform id+tenantId defense-in-depth pattern is missing from six write paths
findings.detail: approveByQuorum (251-257) and escalateToHuman (258-261) UPDATE schema.approvals by `eq(approvals.id, approvalId)` only; setObjectiveStatus (171-175) updates objectives by id only; lease release (359-364) and renew (365-372) update agent_leases by id only; and the reads that feed them (loadObjective 93-97, loadProposal 218-222, loadVotes 240-244) are also unscoped. Phase 68 CR-03 established the project standard that every admin/sink write carries `id AND tenantId` as defense-in-depth precisely because these ids flow through JSONB-shaped queues and future callers; the CR-01 fix added assertTenant for INSERT/emit paths but left these UPDATE-by-id paths bare. When the operator wires these sinks (the file's stated purpose, 'on db-up'), runCriticReview(approvalId) called with a cross-tenant approvalId will happily flip another tenant's approval to decided_via='critic_quorum' — the sink contract carries no caller-tenant assertion, and the service-role connection bypasses RLS. Not exploitable today only because the sinks remain unwired.
findings.fix_sketch: loadProposal/loadObjective already return the row's tenantId — thread it to the write calls and add `and(eq(...id), eq(...tenantId, tenantId))` on approveByQuorum, escalateToHuman, setObjectiveStatus, release, and renew, returning/throwing loudly when 0 rows match (mirror the manager-decide 409 shape at apps/api/src/index.ts:1633-1635). Alternatively add an expectedTenantId parameter to the sink contract so the pure modules pass the tenant they loaded.

findings.summary: POST /api/connections/:mcpId/credential is not admin-gated — runner and external API keys can overwrite tenant MCP OAuth credentials
findings.detail: Every credential-shaped admin surface uses requireAdmin, but this endpoint (apps/api/src/index.ts:1712-1728) sits under only the generic /api/* verifyApiKey middleware, so keys of kind 'runner' or 'external' (ApiKeyContext kinds at packages/core/src/auth.ts:13) can call it. A runner key — distributed to every runner host — or a least-privilege external key can replace the tenant's stored accessToken/refreshToken for any MCP in the tenant via storeCredential. That lets a compromised runner host or leaked external key silently repoint a connector (e.g. swap the Close CRM credential for an attacker-controlled account) so every subsequent agent run exfiltrates tenant data to the attacker's SaaS account. Within-tenant, so not a cross-tenant break, but it is a secret-handling privilege escalation on the exact surface (vault credentials) the doctrine treats as highest-stakes. GET /api/connections (1692) is metadata-only and fine.
findings.fix_sketch: Add requireAdmin to the route: `app.post("/api/connections/:mcpId/credential", requireAdmin, async (c) => ...)`. If the future OAuth-callback flow needs a non-admin path, mint a dedicated key kind ('oauth_callback') instead of leaving it open to runner/external keys, and emit a relay event (e.g. connector.credential_stored) for the audit trail on every write.

findings.summary: Handoff sink is the only V2 sink without the assertTenant tripwire; runHandoff emits refusal events with unvalidated request.tenantId
findings.detail: The CR-01 tripwire contract (lifecycle-sinks.ts:45-49) states 'every V2 sink must resolve a real tenantId before inserting a row or emitting a relay event', and every other sink calls assertTenant. buildHandoffSink.queueHandoff (440-465) inserts runs + agent_handoffs and emit (467-483) writes relay events using input.request.tenantId / input.target.tenantId with no assertTenant. The queue path is indirectly safe (decideHandoff at a2a.ts:87 refuses tenant mismatches, and resolveTarget is DB-scoped), but runHandoff (a2a.ts:179) calls sink.emit for ALL decisions including refusals — so a caller regression that passes an empty-string request.tenantId flows straight into relay_events with tenantId '' (refuse_unknown path: resolveTarget('') finds nothing, decideHandoff refuses, emit still fires). That is precisely the empty-bucket poison CR-01's tripwire was built to stop, and relay emit() (packages/core/src/relay/emit.ts:47-57) performs no tenantId validation of its own.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `assertTenant(input.request.tenantId)` at the top of both queueHandoff and the handoff sink's emit (and optionally assert request.tenantId === target.tenantId in queueHandoff). One line each, restores the uniform tripwire.

findings.summary: Platform-owner gate on GET /api/admin/models is bypassable read-wise: /models/recommend, /models/forecast, and /chat/dispatch return the full platform catalog to any tenant admin
findings.detail: GET /api/admin/models (684) and the proposals endpoints are requirePlatformOwner-gated because 'platform-global tables must NOT be exposed to per-tenant admin keys' (comment at 140-149). But POST /api/admin/models/recommend (698), /models/forecast (930), and /chat/dispatch (746) are requireAdmin only and return pickBestModel/compareForecasts output — ranked candidates plus the `filtered` list with per-slug reasons — computed over the entire loadModelCatalog(db) result. Any tenant admin can enumerate every catalog slug, capability score and cost posture by posting a permissive TaskProfile, making the read half of the platform-owner gate ineffective. The write half (proposals/decide, models mutation) is correctly gated, so this is an inconsistency rather than a live exploit: decide whether catalog reads are tenant-visible (then the gate on GET /models is unnecessary friction) or platform-private (then recommend/forecast responses leak).
findings.fix_sketch: Pick one posture. Either (a) relax GET /api/admin/models to requireAdmin and document the catalog as tenant-visible read-only, or (b) trim the recommend/forecast/chat-dispatch responses to only the winning pick plus anonymized candidate count for non-platform tenants (strip `filtered` and full candidate arrays).

findings.summary: lead_events is documented append-only but its RLS modify policy is FOR ALL — tenant members can UPDATE/DELETE audit-log rows
findings.detail: The table comment (0032:120-121) declares 'ordered audit log per lead. Append-only; no UPDATE/DELETE expected', yet lead_events_modify_own_tenant (167-169) is `FOR ALL ... USING/WITH CHECK (tenant member)`, so any authenticated tenant member connecting through Supabase (anon/authenticated role paths, not the service-role API) can rewrite or delete lead_events history — e.g. erase a 'suppressed' or 'scored' event trail. All the sibling 0026-0032 tables genuinely need UPDATE (status transitions), so their FOR ALL policies are correct; lead_events is the one table whose declared contract is narrower than its policy. This is the only RLS/intent drift found in the 0026-0032 range — the policy *shape* itself (SELECT policy + FOR ALL policy over tenant_members) is uniform across all seven migrations.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the FOR ALL policy on lead_events with `FOR INSERT ... WITH CHECK (tenant member)` (keep the SELECT policy). If operators ever need corrections, do them via the service-role API where they are audited, not via member-session UPDATEs. Same consideration optionally applies to relay_events if its policy shares the shape.

findings.summary: Deferred Phase 69 IN-02: CJS require('@agent-os/db') inside the lazy DB getter — ESM migration landmine; the stated lazy-load rationale is invalid
findings.detail: createDbLazy (764-770) still uses `require("@agent-os/db")` behind an eslint-disable, in an otherwise-ESM module. custom-tools.ts was already fixed (it now imports createDb at top, line 44, and its getDb at 73-79 uses it), so lead-pipeline-tools.ts is the last holdout of the pattern Phase 69 IN-02 deferred. The justification comment ('kept lazy so the module doesn't require DATABASE_URL at import time') is incorrect: importing the createDb function reads no env — only calling it does, and getDb() already defers the call. Under the planned strict-ESM/Node 22 pass, bare require in ESM is a ReferenceError, and this file would break at first tool dispatch.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `createDb` to the existing top-of-file import from "@agent-os/db" (line 19), change getDb() to call it directly, and delete createDbLazy plus its eslint-disable. Keep the lazy `_db` singleton — that part is correct.

findings.summary: apifyRunActor's CR-01 matrix gate is skipped entirely for actor ids not in DISCOVERY_ACTORS — unknown actors dispatch to Apify with no ICP check and a default cap of 100, re-opening the Phase 69 CR-01 hole.
findings.detail: The gate is wrapped in `if (matrixActor) { ... }` (line 100). When the agent passes any actor_id that is NOT in the catalog (e.g. "apify/website-content-crawler" or a hallucinated org/name), matrixActor is undefined, the entire active-ICP lookup + targets[] refusal is bypassed, `ceiling` defaults to 100, `externalId` falls back to the raw actor_id (line 121), and the request is forwarded to Apify with the operator's APIFY_TOKEN. The discovery prompt (scripts/seed/acqu-discovery-agent.ts:43) promises "The tool loads the active ICP server-side and refuses any actor whose targets[] excludes that target_type — you cannot bypass this" — that claim is false for unregistered actors, which is exactly the off-prompt Hermes-70B failure mode CR-01 was rated critical for. An off-prompt agent can run ANY paid Apify actor. No test covers the unknown-actor path (custom-tools.test.ts only covers updateLead guards).
findings.fix_sketch: Deny by default: after the find(), add `if (!matrixActor) return envErr(`actor ${actor_id} not in DISCOVERY_ACTORS — only registered actors are dispatchable`);` then drop the `?? 100` / `?? actor_id` fallbacks (matrixActor is now guaranteed). Update the enrichment-scoring seed if it relies on any un-catalogued actor (it does not — Section 3 only names catalogued keys).

findings.summary: update_lead writes agent-supplied `qualified: true` verbatim with no server-side hard-disqualifier check — a DNC'd or invalid-email lead can be marked qualified, defeating the doctrine rule that only exists in a pure helper no runtime path calls.
findings.detail: Doctrine at packages/core/src/lead-pipeline.ts:13 says "DNC or invalid email always disqualifies, regardless of score." That rule is implemented only in applyQualificationRules(), which is exported and unit-tested but never invoked by any runtime path (grep confirms callers are lead-pipeline.test.ts and index.ts re-export only). Enforcement is delegated entirely to the Hermes-70B agent's prompt (acqu-enrichment-scoring.ts:71). updateLead (line 501: `if (hasQualified) patch.qualified = raw.qualified as boolean;`) accepts qualified=true even when the same payload carries dnc_flag=true, and never consults the row's existing dnc_flag/email_status. An off-prompt agent can flip an opted-out contact to qualified=true; the row lands in `leads_tenant_qualified_idx WHERE qualified=true`, which is precisely the set outreach will consume — reaching out to a suppressed contact is the compliance scenario the doctrine forbids. Same enforce-only-in-the-pure-helper shape as Phase 69 CR-01.
findings.fix_sketch: In updateLead, before building the patch: compute effective dnc/email state (incoming values falling back to the owner row — extend the ownership SELECT to pull dncFlag + emailStatus), then either force `patch.qualified = false` with a returned notice, or `return envErr("qualified=true refused: dnc_flag/email_status hard disqualifier")` when raw.qualified === true and a hard disqualifier holds. Ideally call applyQualificationRules() here so the contract has one runtime enforcement point.

findings.summary: buildCriticReviewSink.loadProposal hardcodes `estimatedCostUsd: 0` while its own comment says "leave null and isCriticEligible routes to human" — every proposal becomes critic-quorum-eligible, silently disabling the stake-cap safety rule the moment the sink is wired.
findings.detail: The ProposalForReview contract (packages/core/src/critic.ts:59) defines `estimatedCostUsd: number | null; null = unknown`, and isCriticEligible (critic.ts:75-77) treats null as "unknown stake is human-only" — fail-closed. The sink comment (lifecycle-sinks.ts:235-236) states the intent: "until the payload carries it, leave null and isCriticEligible routes to human." The code passes 0 instead, and `0 == null` is false, `0 > maxStakeUsd(5)` is false → every non-cant-fail proposal is ELIGIBLE for peer auto-approval regardless of its true cost. An arbitrarily expensive proposal (the exact case the stake cap exists for) can be quorum-approved without a human. No test exercises the Drizzle sinks (grep for lifecycle-sinks in *.test.ts returns nothing). Same wire-the-sink-and-it-misbehaves class Phase 68 rated critical (CR-01).
findings.fix_sketch: Change line 237 to `estimatedCostUsd: null,` (the type already allows it). When the approvals payload later carries a real estimate, parse it there. One-line fix that restores the documented fail-closed default.

findings.summary: Reflexion sink reads verification verdicts from autonomy_events kinds `verification.passed`/`verification.failed` that no code path ever emits — verificationPassed is permanently null, so a verifier-failed 'done' run still completes its objective.
findings.detail: The WR-01 fix (lifecycle-sinks.ts:122-154) queries autonomy_events for kinds "verification.passed"/"verification.failed". Repo-wide grep shows the only autonomy-event kinds ever recorded are allow, propose, deny, session_end, budget_cap, and "autonomy" (hooks.ts:26,105-118; execute.ts:252; api/index.ts budget path; lifecycle.ts:119,438). The actual verification verdict lives in run_summaries.highlights.verification.passed (per eval/scorecard.ts:21 which reads it from there). Result: the verdicts map is always empty, every AttemptOutcome gets verificationPassed: null, and decideReflexion's `last.verificationPassed !== false` check (objective.ts:109) can never see a false — a run whose verifier failed but that ended status='done' completes the objective. The WR-01 "hollow reflexion" defect is half re-introduced: summaries are now real, verification is still a stub wired to a phantom source.
findings.fix_sketch: In loadAttempts, read the verdict from the run_summaries rows already being fetched: select highlights too, then `verificationPassed: (highlights?.verification as {passed?: boolean})?.passed ?? null`. Alternatively, have the verification step emit the two autonomy-event kinds — but pick one source and delete the other query.

findings.summary: buildReflexionSink.queueFollowupRun silently drops `reflexionContext` — the runs table has no column for it and buildBundle never recomposes it, so attempt N+1 starts with zero carryover and the reflexion retry is a plain re-run.
findings.detail: The ReflexionSink contract (packages/core/src/objective.ts:198-202) promises the follow-up runs row carries "`input` carrying the reflexion context." The implementation inserts tenantId/agentId/status/triggerSource/scheduledFor/objectiveId/attemptNumber only — `input.reflexionContext` is never referenced. The runs schema (packages/db/src/schema.ts:189-212) has no input/context column, and buildBundle (packages/core/src/bundle.ts:102-237) reads neither objectives nor prior attempts. So composeReflexionContext's "what to do differently" block is computed and discarded; the entire P3 value proposition (attempt N+1 starts smarter) does not survive the sink boundary. TS cannot catch this because the parameter is an object property, not an unused variable.
findings.fix_sketch: Either add a `runs.input` (or `runs.context`) text/jsonb column in a migration and write reflexionContext into it, then have buildBundle surface it in the bundle (e.g. append to priorLearnings); or have buildBundle recompose the context from objectives + prior runs when run.objectiveId is set (no schema change, slightly more read work). Update the ReflexionSink doc comment to match whichever lands.

findings.summary: buildHandoffSink.queueHandoff ignores `input.handoffContext`, and buildBundle never reads agent_handoffs — the receiving agent never sees the 'Handoff from X' block or artifact refs, breaking a2a.ts's carryover promise.
findings.detail: HandoffSink.queueHandoff (packages/core/src/a2a.ts:139-143) receives the composed handoffContext ("Persist the handoff row + queue the next run"), and the module header (a2a.ts:16-18) promises "the next run carries the prior step's artifacts forward." The implementation writes runs + agent_handoffs rows (summary + artifactRefs are stored on the handoff row) but never touches input.handoffContext, and buildBundle (packages/core/src/bundle.ts) contains no read of agentHandoffs — so nothing connects the queued nextRun to the handoff record at bundle-build time. The receiving run gets a bare scheduled run with no idea it is step S+1 of a chain; composeHandoffContext output is dead on arrival. Same dropped-context shape as CORR-05.
findings.fix_sketch: In buildBundle, when assembling a run, query agentHandoffs by nextRunId and inject the stored context (either persist handoffContext as a new column on agent_handoffs, or recompose via composeHandoffContext from summary + artifactRefs) into the bundle — priorLearnings or a new `handoff` block. Then the sink can keep its current writes.

findings.summary: updateLead's scoring transition fires regardless of current status — a re-score yanks a lead in in_outreach/replied/bounced/closed back to qualified|disqualified, regressing the migration-0032 lifecycle.
findings.detail: The handler doc (lines 437-441 block) and the P4 prompt (acqu-enrichment-scoring.ts:76) both state the scoring write transitions "enriching → qualified | disqualified." The code (line 508-510) sets `patch.status` whenever icp_score AND qualified are present, with no check of owner.status. Migration 0032's documented lifecycle is new → enriching → qualified/disqualified → in_outreach → replied/bounced (0032:63-64); a scoring call against a lead already in in_outreach (or replied/closed) silently rewinds it — the outreach state is lost, and outreach tooling keying off status would re-pick the lead. The enrichment transition is correctly guarded (`owner.status === "new"` at line 507); the scoring one is not, an asymmetry inside the same function.
findings.fix_sketch: Guard the scoring transition: `if (hasIcpScore && hasQualified && (owner.status === "new" || owner.status === "enriching")) { patch.status = ... }`. Optionally return an envErr when the agent attempts to score a lead already past qualification, so the misbehavior is visible instead of silent.

findings.summary: updateLead validates icp_score as finite-in-[0,100] but not integer, and does not validate email_status/phone_type/dnc_flag at all — values legal to the tool but illegal to migration 0032's INTEGER column and CHECK constraints make the handler THROW instead of returning the {ok:false} envelope.
findings.detail: leads.icp_score is INTEGER CHECK (0..100) (0032:85) and the scoring contract requires an integer (validateScoringResult, lead-pipeline.ts:297 — 50.5 is rejected there and in its test). updateLead accepts 72.5 (line 462-468 checks only Number.isFinite + range), so the drizzle UPDATE sends '72.5' to an int4 column → Postgres 'invalid input syntax' error thrown. Similarly email_status/phone_type are copied through untyped (lines 502-503) though the DB CHECK allows only fixed vocabularies (0032:75,77), and dnc_flag is not checked as boolean (line 504). Any bad value escapes as a thrown exception: dispatchCustomTool rethrows (custom-tools.ts:584-594), violating this file's own envelope doctrine (lines 10-12, 'Never throw... the agent should log + skip') and turning a recoverable agent mistake into a run-level failure. custom-tools.test.ts covers whitelist + out-of-range score only — none of these paths.
findings.fix_sketch: In the pre-DB validation block: require `Number.isInteger(s)` for icp_score (mirroring validateScoringResult); validate email_status against the EmailStatus union and phone_type against PhoneType (both importable from @agent-os/core); require `typeof raw.dnc_flag === "boolean"`. Return envErr for each, keeping the never-throw contract.

findings.summary: P4 prompt claims a scoring-failed lead "stays status='new' for the next batch" — false: step E already transitioned it to 'enriching', and the batch loader filters status='new' only, so scoring-failed leads are orphaned in 'enriching' forever.
findings.detail: The prompt's own flow makes the claim impossible: step E (line 53) instructs update_lead with enrichment BEFORE scoring, which server-derives status new → enriching (lead-pipeline-tools.ts:507). If the tool.delegate scoring step then fails (or the run crashes/hits its budget stop between E and scoring), the lead sits at status='enriching' — but step 2 (line 22) loads batches with `filter: { status: 'new' }` only, and supabaseQuery supports exactly one status value per call (lead-pipeline-tools.ts:242). No agent, endpoint, or cron ever re-reads 'enriching' rows, so those leads never get icp_score/qualified, permanently breaking the prompt's acceptance test 'Every lead has icp_score set' (line 81). This is a real production leak: every transient sub-agent failure permanently removes a paid-for, fully-enriched lead from the pipeline.
findings.fix_sketch: Smallest fix: change step 2 to load status='enriching' first (stalled leads), then fill remaining batch budget with status='new', and update the line-98 claim to "stays status='enriching' and is picked up first next batch." (Requires either two supabase_query calls in the prompt — already supported — or an `in`-filter in the tool.) Alternative: defer the new→enriching transition until scoring succeeds, but that loses the in-progress marker.

findings.summary: apolloSearch has no target-type/ICP gate at all — the discovery prompt says "the runtime tool selects actors using the SAME matrix," but apollo:search (registered mid_market/tech_funded/enterprise-only) dispatches unchecked for local_smb/creator ICPs.
findings.detail: The CR-01 fix added the active-ICP targets[] refusal only to apifyRunActor. tool.discovery.apollo_search — the second discovery dispatch path, catalogued in DISCOVERY_ACTORS as `apollo:search` with targets [mid_market, tech_funded, enterprise] (lead-pipeline.ts:124-130) — performs zero matrix enforcement: it clamps per_page and forwards to Apollo (lines 163-203). The discovery prompt's Section 2 (acqu-discovery-agent.ts:69) claims runtime selection uses "the SAME matrix"; for this tool that is false. A local_smb or creator tenant's off-prompt agent burns Apollo API spend on a source the matrix excludes, and inserts leads whose source_actor contradicts the matrix doctrine (lead-pipeline.ts:12).
findings.fix_sketch: Extract the active-ICP lookup + targets check from apifyRunActor into a shared helper `assertActorAllowedForActiveIcp(db, tenantId, actorKey)` and call it at the top of apolloSearch with the fixed key "apollo:search". Same refusal envelope as the apify path.

findings.summary: Duplicate terminal status post is NOT the no-op the comment claims: composeRunSummary's plain insert hits run_summaries.run_id UNIQUE and 500s the retried request; no transition guard exists anywhere on the live path (validRunTransition is exported but never called).
findings.detail: lifecycle.ts:110-112 promises "a duplicate terminal-status post (network retry) is a no-op on the Relay side too" — the relay emit is eventKey-idempotent, but the same tx then inserts a second session_end and re-runs composeRunSummary, whose insert (packages/core/src/relay/summary.ts:107-130, no onConflict) violates run_summaries.run_id UNIQUE (schema.ts:527-530) → whole tx rolls back → setRunStatus throws → PUT /api/runs/:id/status returns 500. So the exact scenario the comment anticipates (runner retries after a dropped response) fails loudly every time, and the runner cannot distinguish 'already terminal, all good' from a real failure. Compounding: the endpoint (apps/api/src/index.ts:225-231) validates only status membership, never the transition — dispatch-contract.ts's validRunTransition state machine has zero production callers (grep confirms only the index.ts re-export), so done→running resurrection is also accepted. integration.test.ts covers a single terminal post only.
findings.fix_sketch: In setRunStatus, read the current row first (the tx already updates-returning — select before update) and short-circuit: if current status is terminal and update.status equals it, return the row unchanged (idempotent success); if terminal and different, refuse. Better: gate every transition with validRunTransition(current, next) and 409 on violation — that makes the offline contract the live contract.

findings.summary: buildReflexionSink.loadAttempts loads ALL runs for the objective regardless of status and force-casts runs.status into AttemptOutcome's 5-value union — a concurrent scheduled/waiting/pending run counts as a failed attempt in decideReflexion.
findings.detail: The query (lines 110-118) has no status filter; line 160 casts r.status (7-value RUN_STATUSES world: scheduled/running/done/failed/skipped/waiting/pending) into AttemptOutcome["status"] ("done|failed|escalated|skipped|quarantined" — which itself mirrors run_summaries.status, not RUN_STATUSES; "escalated"/"quarantined" never occur on runs rows, per shared/enums.ts:22-31). A non-terminal run bound to the same objective (e.g. an operator-created manual run, or a race with a just-queued follow-up) flows into decideReflexion where anything !== 'done' takes the failure path (objective.ts:110-133) — burning an attempt slot toward maxAttempts or triggering a duplicate retry. Low likelihood today because attempts are sequential and the sink is not yet wired, but the cast hides the type drift from the compiler permanently.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `inArray(schema.runs.status, ["done", "failed", "skipped"])` to the loadAttempts where-clause, and align AttemptOutcome["status"] with the statuses that can actually appear (or document explicitly that it mirrors run_summaries.status, then map instead of cast).

findings.summary: buildHandoffSink.emit (and queueHandoff) is the only V2 sink without the CR-01 assertTenant tripwire — refuse_* decisions emit relay events with caller-supplied request.tenantId unchecked.
findings.detail: Every other sink calls assertTenant before writes/emits (reflexion: lines 179,196; critic: 265; lease: 308,341,375; improvement: 501,524,543; manager: 574,590,603,617). buildHandoffSink.emit fires for ALL decisions including refuse_unknown/refuse_cross_tenant, where the target row (the only DB-verified tenant source) is null — so an empty-string request.tenantId from a regressed caller reaches the relay emit unchecked, the exact poisoned-bucket scenario the Phase 68 CR-01 tripwire exists to fail loudly on. queueHandoff is de-facto safe (decideHandoff guarantees target.tenantId === request.tenantId before queue), but the emit path is not.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `assertTenant(input.request.tenantId);` as the first line of buildHandoffSink.emit (and optionally in queueHandoff for uniformity). One-liner each, restores the every-sink invariant stated in the assertTenant doc comment (lines 45-49).

findings.summary: retryRun clones a run without objectiveId/attemptNumber — a manual retry of an objective-bound attempt detaches from its objective, so its outcome never feeds reflexion and the objective idles until abandoned.
findings.detail: retryRun (lines 199-214) predates migration 0026's objective columns and copies tenantId/agentId/jobId only; the clone gets objectiveId=null and attemptNumber=1 (defaults). When an operator retries a failed attempt of a multi-run objective, the retry's terminal outcome is invisible to runReflexion (keyed on runs.objectiveId), the objective's attempt history is silently forked, and the reflexion loop may later queue its own duplicate retry of the same work. Contract drift between the P3 objective model and the pre-P3 retry helper.
findings.fix_sketch: Copy `objectiveId: orig.objectiveId` and, when set, `attemptNumber: orig.attemptNumber + 1` into the clone (or refuse manual retry on objective-bound runs and point the operator at the reflexion loop). Decide deliberately which — either is better than silent detachment.

findings.summary: applyQualificationRules has no finite-number guard: a NaN score bypasses the threshold rule (NaN < threshold is false) and falls through to the scorer's qualified flag — NaN-scored leads can qualify.
findings.detail: The function is exported as the final qualification authority ("DNC or invalid email always wins") but trusts score/scoreThreshold blindly. With score=NaN (or scoreThreshold=NaN), line 337's `input.score < input.scoreThreshold` is false, so control reaches the trust-the-scorer branch and returns modelQualified — i.e. a garbage score qualifies a lead whenever the model said yes. validateScoringResult does guard NaN, but nothing forces callers through it (and today no runtime path calls either function — the contract is prompt-enforced only, see CORR-02). lead-pipeline.test.ts has boundary tests (score==threshold) but no NaN case. Flagged because the task dimension explicitly probes the NaN edge and the guard is one line.
findings.fix_sketch: First line of applyQualificationRules: `if (!Number.isFinite(input.score) || !Number.isFinite(input.scoreThreshold)) return { qualified: false, reason: "non-finite score/threshold — refusing to qualify" };` plus a test asserting NaN disqualifies.

findings.summary: mapVerifierResult can never return 'risky' or 'role' despite declaring them in its return type — and the P4 prompt tells the agent email_verify returns those statuses, promising values the tool cannot produce.
findings.detail: The switch (lines 673-683) maps NeverBounce's actual v4 vocabulary (valid/invalid/disposable/catchall/unknown); 'risky' and 'role' appear only in the return-type union and in the prompt's claim at acqu-enrichment-scoring.ts:36 ("returns { status: 'valid'|'risky'|'invalid'|'catchall'|'role'|'unknown' }"). The leads.email_status CHECK allows them (0032:75), so nothing crashes, but the agent is told to expect and branch on statuses that never arrive; role-account detection (NeverBounce reports it via flags like 'role_account', which the handler does return) is silently unreachable via status. Prompt/tool contract drift, cosmetic-to-minor.
findings.fix_sketch: Either map flags: if `j?.flags?.includes("role_account")` return "role", and map "disposable" to "risky" instead of "invalid" if that distinction is wanted; or shrink the return union + prompt claim to the five values actually produced. Keep prompt and mapper in lockstep.

findings.summary: Improvement and manager sinks remain hollow — loadObservations (line 506) and loadFleet (line 564) return [] — so P6 self-improvement and P8 manager cycles are guaranteed no-ops when the operator wires the sinks per this file's own header instructions.
findings.detail: The file header (lines 12-34) presents all six builders as the operator's wire-ready production sinks ("this file ships the actual Drizzle-backed sinks the operator wires into lifecycle.ts on db-up"), and Phase 68's WR-01 fix made reflexion real — but buildImprovementSink.loadObservations and buildManagerSink.loadFleet still return empty arrays behind one-line "Operator: ... Stub returns empty" comments. runSelfImprovement will never find a recurring lesson and runManagerCycle will never see a fleet sample, so wiring them produces silently-dead features (no error, no relay event, nothing). Not previously itemized (Phase 68 WR-01 covered only loadAttempts); reporting so the launch checklist can either implement the joins or explicitly gate these two builders.
findings.fix_sketch: Implement loadObservations (join run_summaries/extracted lessons per improve.ts's Observation contract) and loadFleet (agents joined with trailing scorecard + spend metrics per AgentFleetSample); or, if deferred past launch, make both throw 'not implemented — do not wire' instead of returning [], so wiring them fails loudly like assertTenant does.

findings.summary: Phase 69 deferred IN-02: createDbLazy still uses CJS `require("@agent-os/db")` inside an ESM module — doubly pointless now since the module already statically imports from @agent-os/db at line 19, and the 'mirrors custom-tools' comment is stale (custom-tools.ts imports createDb at top level).
findings.detail: Lines 764-770: `const { createDb } = require("@agent-os/db") ...` survives only via tsx/esbuild's CJS shim and breaks under strict ESM (the planned Node 22 cleanup). The stated rationale — avoid requiring DATABASE_URL at import time — never held: importing createDb reads no env (only calling it does), and the file already has `import { schema, type Db } from "@agent-os/db"` at the top, so the package is statically loaded regardless. The comment at line 755 ("mirrors the pattern used by the rest of custom-tools") is now false: custom-tools.ts:72-79 uses a top-level `createDb` import with the same lazy singleton. This is the exact cleanup Phase 69 IN-02 deferred.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `createDb` to the existing top-level import from "@agent-os/db", change getDb() to call it directly, delete createDbLazy and its eslint-disable + stale comments (~10 lines).

findings.summary: Stale comment: "Operator stub: this would import from architect/hydrate.ts" — the function below it actually does exactly that; it is no longer a stub.
findings.detail: Lines 284-286 describe isAgentCantFail as an operator stub that "would" import from architect/hydrate.ts, but the implementation (lines 287-290) performs the real dynamic import and calls isCantFail. A reader auditing which sinks are still hollow (see CORR-17) is misled into thinking cant-fail resolution is fake. The second sentence (lazy import to avoid circular deps) is the part worth keeping.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the comment with: "Lazy dynamic import of architect/hydrate.ts to avoid a top-level circular dependency; resolves CANT_FAIL_KEYS membership for a live agent key."
